title: Collect a parallel stream without a shared container

blocks.text: In a parallel stream several threads run the lambdas at once, so a lambda that adds to one shared list races with the others. `collect` avoids that: each chunk fills its own container and the containers are merged afterwards, left before right, so encounter order survives as well.
Write two static methods in `SafeCollect`. Each receives a stream that may be sequential or parallel:

items: `List<Long> squares(Stream<Integer> numbers)`: each number squared, as a `long`, in encounter order.
`Map<Character, List<String>> byFirstLetter(Stream<String> words)`: the words grouped by their first letter, each group in encounter order.

blocks.text: The tests also hand both methods large parallel streams and compare the whole result, order included.

cases.says: It squares the numbers and groups the words of a sequential stream.
A parallel stream's squares arrive complete and in encounter order: a shared list filled by forEach loses both.
Each group of a parallel stream keeps encounter order: groupingBy merges per-chunk maps in order, a concurrent grouping does not.
Words that start with the same accented letter share one group: letters are compared with equals, and only small Characters are cached so that == happens to work.
Squares of a parallel stream arrive in encounter order: a synchronized shared list is thread-safe, but forEach still adds in whatever order the threads run.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: collect is safe in parallel because each chunk fills its own container and the containers are merged in order.
A lambda that adds to a shared container races with the other threads of a parallel stream.
